BLOCKER: AC-1 base-area completeness is not enforced: `_area_problems` validates only supplied rows and never requires the documented base areas (security, tenant/RLS, observability, rollback, evidence); a pack with one area passes.
AC-5 is unmet: no test covers `design_pack._area_problems`/`check` area-completeness or the block path; new tests only cover `design_delta_fields` and prompt text.
AC-4 inference/taxonomy is not implemented: there is no area inference from the work item and no extensible taxonomy wiring; `design_areas` remains manual-only.
MAJOR: `_area_problems` hardcodes `{"APPLICABLE","N/A"}` instead of using `config/design-pack.json.area_statuses`; extending taxonomy will be rejected by the gate, defeating AC-4 and duplicating config.
`_areas_enforced` fails open: missing/invalid `areas_enforce_from` or missing `created_at` silently disables area enforcement, so blank design packs can pass.
N/A reasons are only checked for non-empty text; placeholders like `"N/A"`/`"none"` pass, so AC-2 “unexplained N/A” is not enforced.
`sections`/`evidence` elements are not validated; `[""]` passes and non-list rows can crash `_areas` during render, so blank/malformed evidence is not blocked.
Review JSON observability contract is not implemented deterministically: no code records `design_sha`, changed fields, or `review_scope: delta`; this relies on LLM output/prompt text only.
MINOR: `_area_problems` requires `reason` for APPLICABLE too, which is stricter than AC-1 and can reject otherwise valid packs.
Delta prompt still embeds the full design body as context; scoping is instruction-only, not structural, and the doc’s “prompt must include only changed fields” is not literally met.
Prior findings are appended after the delta block; AC-3 says verify prior findings first, but prompt ordering/test coverage does not assert that.
No test covers `_areas_enforced` cutoff, `_item_at` failure fallback, or out-of-scope tagging behavior.
NIT: `_areas` renders the status separator as `?` instead of a proper glyph.
`_item_at` silently swallows all exceptions without logging the fallback path.
Duplicate area names are not detected.
SUMMARY: The diff moves docs/config and prompt text in the right direction, but the gate implementation is incomplete: base areas, real inference/taxonomy, and unexplained-N/A rejection are not enforced.
The largest risk is false confidence: AC-5 tests do not exercise the design-pack gate, so area-completeness can regress unnoticed.
Observability and extensibility promises are not backed by deterministic code.
